messages:
alex: Heads-up — the eu-west GPU dashboard is spamming alerts during nightly stress tests. Lots of thermal / power spikes on panels 42/43. Pager noise is through the roof. anyone else seeing this?

sophia: I saw it too. Most are short spikes (30–90s) that shouldn't page. Alerts look like they have 1m eval + no `for` window.

mario: Can we debounce at the alert level? I think critical should be sustained 10m, warning 3m. Also we should smooth the panel query to avoid visual noise.

alex: Agreed. Current alert rule (approx):
```yaml
- alert: GpuHighTemp
  expr: nvidia_gpu_temp_celsius > 85
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: High GPU temp on {{ $labels.instance }}
```
No `for:` right now.

cass: For Prometheus alerts add `for: 10m` for critical. For warning use `for: 3m` and severity=warning. That alone will cut noise by ~80%.

jen: For panels, use `avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_temp_celsius[5m])` or Grafana's movingAverage transform. Also drop panel resolution to 1m to avoid every single sample showing.

infra-bot: Deploy job started: prometheus/rules/update (job id: 2026-03-18-11)

mario: Proposed alert rule (PromQL):
```
avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_temp_celsius{region="eu-west"}[5m]) > 80
```
and then in Alertmanager set a grouping_interval to 5m so we don't get floods per instance.

cass: Also consider replacing equality >85 with `> bool 85`? not necessary here. More important: use `unless` to suppress during maintenance windows and add `on(instance)` grouping.

alex: Another issue: the panel shows panels 42/43 as separate per-GPU; when one node gets stressed it creates dozens of lines. Maybe switch heatmap or use per-host aggregation.

jen: Heatmap suggestion: use `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(nvidia_gpu_power_watts_bucket[5m])) by (le, host))` — not exact, but a 95th percentile view would hide micro spikes.

cass: For Grafana alerting, set evaluation interval to 1m and require `for: 10m` on critical rule. If using Grafana's new unified alerting, enable `Reduce: mean()` then `Condition: IS ABOVE 80 for 10m` to avoid spike-triggered notifications.

alex: Can someone PR the rules? I'll test changes against the staging alertmanager.

mario: I'll do the Prometheus rule PR. Plan: add `for:` windows, change expr to `avg_over_time(...[5m])`, group alerts by `alertname, instance`, update alertmanager grouping_interval to 5m.

infra-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood.ai/prometheus/+/4321 — mario — pending review

cass: I'll update the Grafana panel: change query to `avg_over_time` and add a transform for 5m rolling mean. Also change panel visualization to heatmap and add annotation for nightly stress tests (ann id: stress-eu-west).

jen: Can we also add an SLO-style dashboard for GPU fleet: 99th tail temp, sustained critical minutes, and cost-per-hour? helps PM and SRE prioritize.

alex: Yes — create a lightweight SLO dashboard that pulls `gpu_sustained_critical_minutes_total` (or compute from alerts fired). Good for monthly reporting.

mario: Updated PR merged to staging. infra-bot: deployment?

infra-bot: Prometheus rules pushed to staging at 1762506865. Alertmanager group_interval temporarily set to 5m for staging.

cass: Pushed Grafana panel changes to staging dashboard (id: 3102). Reduced legend clutter and added `display name = {{host}}:GPU{{gpu_id}}` formatting.

alex: Nice. Any remaining pager noise?

jen: Slightly quieter. We still see a couple of sustained nodes during long tests — those are genuine. Alerts are far less noisy though. :thumbsup:

mario: I'll schedule a follow-up to run one more full-night test tomorrow and collect SLO deltas.

alex: Thanks all — leaving this thread open until tomorrow morning to confirm.

cass: If it looks stable by 10:00 UTC, I'll replicate the rule change to prod and update runbook.

infra-bot: Job complete: deploy/prometheus-rules -> staging -> success (1762506915)

alex: closing in AM unless new alerts show up.
